log.msg: inventoried Servex MCP, site MCP, in-process SDK tools, node CLI scripts and hooks
traced task-creation, prompt-handling, transcription flows; found session_id/landed_at/hold --paths as the AI steps that actually break, with evidence from the minion skill's own incident notes

outcome: Audit done. Report at public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/servex-mastermind/audit/tools/report.md: four tables (Tools, Flows, Top 6, Harness) plus 3 findings, 63 lines. Top finding: the riskiest AI-only steps (session_id on task launch, landed_at target, hold --paths) already have a node tool nearby that could just refuse the bad call; those are the cheapest wins. A harness switch off Claude Code breaks new-task and the prompt-relay hook outright — MCP reachability to Servex from a non-Claude-Code harness is unverified and is the one thing worth checking before trusting it.
